idea: China macro and policy briefing for Western allocators
buyer: Allocators and macro PMs with China exposure decisions
pain: China commentary is either propaganda or hostile, rarely useful
v1: A monthly briefing with primary-source policy reading
verdict: Genuine differentiation via primary sources, but the price point demands an audience she lacks.

why.distribution: Some warm readers, but seat-based subscriptions need a wider audience than her network.
why.demand: Inferred; there is abundant free China commentary of varying quality.
why.fmf: Language, policy access and investment framing - genuinely differentiated versus most Western commentary.
why.defensibility: Primary-source access via her father's network is hard to replicate.
why.tailwind: China matters enormously but allocator appetite for China exposure has fallen.
why.ceiling: £400/mo x 42 seats = £202k, needing 42 paying institutional seats from a standing start.

ceiling_arithmetic: £400/mo x 42 seats = £202k. Forty-two paying seats implies an audience of ~1,000 engaged professionals, built from zero. Realistic: 10-15 seats = £48-72k.
carries: Real primary-source differentiation in a field of secondhand commentary, with full media leverage.
kills: Audience from zero, and Western allocator appetite for China is currently shrinking.
test: Publish three briefings free and see whether institutional readers ask for more.
test_pass: Several ask about a paid tier.
